sheet-1.description: This part is the lower half of sheet 1, drawn at 100 ft to an inch below a heavy line that separates it from the key map, index and water facilities notes of the atlas. It covers the area north of the business district between the Erie Railroad tracks at the left edge and Island Avenue at the right, from Chestnut along the top to Carrol along the bottom. Church runs north and south down the left side of the part, crossed by Cedar in its lower half; Central Avenue leaves the top left corner diagonally beside the railroad; Weems Place, marked arbitrary, runs south from Cedar to Carrol; and Poplar Street leaves Island Avenue to the east near the bottom right. A trolley right-of-way runs north and south through the middle of the part. The land is mostly in large lots: frame dwellings line Church, Chestnut and Island Avenue, while the big block numbered 13 between Weems Place and the trolley line is nearly empty. Buildings of note are the E. T. Laroe coal and feed shed beside the railroad at Cedar, the Lutheran Church on Church at Carrol, and The Howard House on the east side of the trolley line near Carrol. A scale bar sits in the lower middle, and the sheet numbers of the adjoining sheets 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 are printed around the edges.
notes: The upper half of the sheet holds the key map at 1000 ft to an inch, the key, the index and the water facilities and fire department notes; only the lower half is georeferenced.
Weems Place is marked arbitrary on the sheet; it is North Spruce Street today. Carrol is Carol Street.
Island Avenue is Island Avenue north of Poplar Street and North Island Avenue south of it in OpenStreetMap.

Key map of the town at 1000 ft to an inch, key, index and water facilities in the upper half (not configured: key map, too small a scale); lower half is a map at 100 ft: Chestnut, Church, Cedar, Weems Pl (arbitrary), Carrol, Central Av, Island Av, Poplar St, trolley right-of-way, Erie R.R. One configured part (lower half). Result: 6 automatic points, RMSE 2.0 m, LOO 4.3 m.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and shows the centre of Ramsey on both sides of the Erie Railroad main line, which runs north and south through the middle of the sheet with several tracks and a siding. Main crosses the sheet from west to east just above the middle. West of the railroad, Central Avenue runs north and south near the left edge and Maple south of Main, with High School Place leaving Central Avenue to the east in the upper part; east of the railroad, Church runs north from Main to Carrol Street at the top, and Mechanic runs south from Main at the right edge. North of Main west of the tracks are Central Hall, a few dwellings, the fire department building, a bowling alley and a gate tower; south of Main are the post office and a drug store and a row of stores, with dwellings along Maple and Central Avenue. Beside the tracks south of Main stand the Erie Railroad station, a waiting shelter, a freight house, an old shed on the railroad siding, a wagon shed and a switch tower. East of the tracks are the Ramsey Hotel on Church at Main, sheds and a water tower with an electric motor, and on the south side of Main a row of brick stores including The Ramsey Journal printing office and a plumber, with store houses, a club and dwellings along Mechanic. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are drawn in the streets; two short streets at the left edge are marked no name.
notes: Central Avenue is North Central Avenue north of Main and South Central Avenue south of it in OpenStreetMap; Main is West Main Street west of the railroad and East Main Street east of it.
High School Place is School Street in OpenStreetMap; Carrol Street is Carol Street.
Two short streets at the left edge are lettered 'No Name'.
Scale 50 ft to an inch, twice that of most sheets of the atlas.

Scale 50 ft to an inch. Business district west and east of the Erie R.R.: Main, Central Av, Maple, High School Pl, Church, Carrol St, Mechanic; Erie R.R. station. Result: 5 automatic + 1 hand-picked (Carrol/Church), RMSE 1.6 m; points mostly along Main, so LOO is not meaningful.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and shows the eastern half of the Ramsey business district, from Church at the left edge to the trolley right-of-way and a brook at the right. Carrol runs along the top, Main crosses the sheet just above the middle, and Arch leaves Main diagonally to the north-east. South of Main, Mechanic runs down the left side and Prospect runs south from Main and then turns east across the lower right of the sheet. The north side of Main is lined with frame stores, the Hotel Bergen, a cobbler, two bakeries with a portable oven, an ice cream factory with a hall above, a hardware and crockery store and storage sheds; behind them on Church are a livery stable and wagon house and, at the corner of Carrol, an electric transformer station. Between Arch and the trolley line stand brick-faced bowling alleys and a moving picture theatre, both on piles, and a building marked to be tenements. South of Main are a row of stores, the First National Bank, and on the east a hall, a blacksmith and a warehouse with tenements and a garage; the blocks along Mechanic and Prospect hold dwellings on deep lots, and much of the block east of Prospect, numbered 16, is open. The part west of Mechanic is left blank and refers to sheet 2. A brook, drawn in blue, runs south along the trolley right-of-way at the right edge.
notes: Carrol is Carol Street in OpenStreetMap; Main is East Main Street.

The north-south stretch of Prospect south of Main is North Spruce Street today; the diagonal stretch east of the corner is Prospect Street. Modern North Spruce Street continues north of Main, which the sheet does not show.
Only the south side of Carrol is drawn at the top edge.
Scale 50 ft to an inch.

Scale 50 ft to an inch. Business district east: Church, Carrol, Main, Arch, Mechanic, Prospect; trolley right-of-way and brook at the east edge. Result: 3 automatic + 2 hand-picked, RMSE 1.3 m; fitted 7.73 px/ft (about 3 percent under sheet 2), so scale_ft 51.5 is set to keep its own scale in the second pass. About 4 m step against sheet 7 on Main at the trolley line.

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 4 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and covering the north end of Ramsey between the Erie Railroad main line at the left edge and the Turnpike at the upper right. Island Avenue crosses the railroad at the left and runs diagonally down to a junction beside a small pond, where Spring leaves it to run north-east to the Turnpike; a brook runs from the upper left down to the pond. Grant runs north and south through the upper middle, Orchard crosses the top and turns south, Koch Street appears at the top, and the trolley right-of-way runs diagonally from the top down across Spring. The area is laid out in long, thinly built lots in blocks 7A to 7D, 18 and 20, with frame dwellings and outbuildings along Grant, Spring and Island Avenue and a green house and a hen house on Island Avenue. The yard of the Ramsey Lumber Co. with its lumber sheds lies beside the railroad at the lower left. The water works inset of part 2 occupies the lower right corner and the turned strip of part 3 lies below a heavy line at the bottom.
notes: Island Avenue north-west of Spring is Island Road in OpenStreetMap, and the Turnpike is Franklin Turnpike.

The area was rebuilt for Route 17: the junction of Island Avenue and Spring, Spring's east end and Island Avenue's railroad crossing no longer follow their 1924 lines, and Grant and Orchard survive only in part or not at all.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (Spring and the Turnpike) and a point on the railroad main line whose latitude assumes the sheet's north at 7 degrees; the placement is low confidence, perhaps 10 to 20 m off.
Ramsey Lumber Co. lumber sheds beside the railroad.

Scale 100 ft. Three parts: part 1 (main, upper left) Island Av, Spring, Grant, Orchard, Koch St, Turnpike, Erie R.R. (main line), Ramsey Lumber Co.; part 2 (inset, right) Ramsey Water Works with Island Av and a street 'Not Named'; part 3 (lower strip, turned, north to the upper right) Crescent Av, Wycoff Av, Cedar, Forest Av, Sniders Rd. Result: part 1 low confidence (Route 17 rebuilt Island Av./Spring): helmert from Spring/Turnpike and a point on the Erie main line, perhaps 10 to 20 m off. Part 2 (water works inset) not placed. Part 3 helmert from four junctions along Wycoff Av. (one hand-picked).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Ramsey Water Works (pump house, wells), with Island Av. and a street lettered 'Not Named' (one junction, with an unnamed street that could not be identified among modern streets; the inset lies outside the reference of the other parts; needs identification of the unnamed street (possibly near Island Road at the north borough line), then an anchored fit with px_per_ft about 4.0 and north_deg 0).

sheet-4-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 4 is the strip below the heavy line at the bottom of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right, as on sheet 5. It covers the south-western end of Ramsey along Wycoff Avenue, which crosses the strip from left to right in its lower part, from Crescent Avenue at the left, past Forest Avenue and Cedar, to Sniders Road at the right edge. Crescent Avenue comes down to Wycoff Avenue from the upper left, beside a dash-dot boundary line that continues south across the avenue; Cedar runs north from Wycoff Avenue and Forest Avenue south from it. The area is thinly settled: frame dwellings, a few concrete block houses and hen houses stand on long lots either side of Wycoff Avenue, with the largest group of narrow house lots along Cedar in block 38, and much of block 32 south of the avenue open. A water pipe runs along Wycoff Avenue, and the number 5 at the right edge refers to the adjoining sheet.
notes: Wycoff Avenue is Wyckoff Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Crescent Avenue is West Crescent Avenue; Cedar is East Cedar Place (West Cedar Place continues it south); Sniders Road is Snyder Avenue.
The dash-dot line lettered boundary line beside Crescent Avenue is the borough line.
Drawn turned about 46 degrees: north points to the upper right of the sheet.
Placed by a helmert fit to four junctions along Wycoff Avenue (one hand-picked), so its position across the avenue rests on the assumed similarity.

Scale 100 ft. Three parts: part 1 (main, upper left) Island Av, Spring, Grant, Orchard, Koch St, Turnpike, Erie R.R. (main line), Ramsey Lumber Co.; part 2 (inset, right) Ramsey Water Works with Island Av and a street 'Not Named'; part 3 (lower strip, turned, north to the upper right) Crescent Av, Wycoff Av, Cedar, Forest Av, Sniders Rd. Result: part 1 low confidence (Route 17 rebuilt Island Av./Spring): helmert from Spring/Turnpike and a point on the Erie main line, perhaps 10 to 20 m off. Part 2 (water works inset) not placed. Part 3 helmert from four junctions along Wycoff Av. (one hand-picked).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Ramsey Water Works (pump house, wells), with Island Av. and a street lettered 'Not Named' (one junction, with an unnamed street that could not be identified among modern streets; the inset lies outside the reference of the other parts; needs identification of the unnamed street (possibly near Island Road at the north borough line), then an anchored fit with px_per_ft about 4.0 and north_deg 0).

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 is the upper part of the sheet, above a heavy V-shaped line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 46 degrees clockwise). It covers the south-western end of Ramsey along Wycoff Avenue, which crosses the part from left to right just above its middle. Snider Road leaves Wycoff Avenue at the left edge and Echo Avenue, marked arbitrary, runs down from it towards the lower middle; Ramsey Avenue runs up to the left from Wycoff Avenue to Franklin, which crosses the upper left, and Oak runs diagonally from the top to Wycoff Avenue at the right. Beyond the dash-dot match line A-B at the right edge the drawing continues as part 2, and Mt. Joy Ct., marked arbitrary, crosses the strip beyond the line. The area is thinly built: frame dwellings, a few stone or concrete block houses and outbuildings stand on long narrow lots along Wycoff Avenue, Ramsey Avenue and Oak, with the house lots between Franklin and Oak laid out in a regular subdivision, while blocks 32, 38 and 60 are large and mostly empty. A small group of house lots south of Wycoff Avenue near Oak is drawn as a separate row of narrow parcels. Water pipes run along Wycoff Avenue, Snider Road and Echo Avenue.
notes: Wycoff Avenue is Wyckoff Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Snider Road is Snyder Avenue; Echo Avenue (marked arbitrary) is Pine Street; Oak is West Oak Street; Franklin is Franklin Street.
Drawn turned about 46 degrees: north points to the upper right of the sheet.
East Oak Street, which today continues Oak south of Wyckoff Avenue, is not drawn.
Placed from three detected and two hand-picked junctions; four of the five lie along Wycoff Avenue, so the fit across the avenue rests on the Franklin and Ramsey Avenue junction.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy V-shaped line: part 1 (upper) Wycoff Av, Franklin, Ramsey Av, Oak, Snider Rd, Echo Av, Woodland Av, Mt Joy Ct; part 2 (lower, turned, north to the upper right) Wycoff Av, Kelleher Av, Mt Joy Ct (arbitrary). Result: part 1 from 3 automatic + 2 hand-picked junctions (4 along Wycoff Av.); part 2 from Kelleher/Wycoff plus 3 points carried from part 1 along match line A-B. Both drawn turned about 46 degrees.

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 is the lower part of the sheet, below a heavy V-shaped line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with the same turn as part 1 (north to the upper right). It continues part 1 to the north-east, joining it along the dash-dot match line A-B at its left edge, and joins sheet 6 along the match line C-D at its right. Wycoff Avenue crosses the part from left to right, curving gently upward, with Kelleher Avenue running down from it near the left and Mt. Joy Ct., marked arbitrary, along the lower left; Woodland Avenue appears at the upper right corner. The heavy dividing line above is lettered no exposure. The built-up corner at the lower left, around Kelleher Avenue and Mt. Joy Ct., holds frame dwellings and several stone and concrete block houses, some with brick fronts; the rest of the part, blocks 32 and 36 on either side of Wycoff Avenue, is open land with a few dwellings and hen houses. A water pipe runs along Wycoff Avenue.
notes: Wycoff Avenue is Wyckoff Avenue in OpenStreetMap. Mt. Joy Ct. (marked arbitrary) may be today's Center Street, but its junction with Kelleher Avenue did not agree with the drawing and was not used.
Drawn on the page beside part 1 rather than where it lies: the match line A-B joins the two parts.
Placed from one street junction (Kelleher Avenue and Wycoff Avenue) and three points carried from part 1 along the match line A-B.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy V-shaped line: part 1 (upper) Wycoff Av, Franklin, Ramsey Av, Oak, Snider Rd, Echo Av, Woodland Av, Mt Joy Ct; part 2 (lower, turned, north to the upper right) Wycoff Av, Kelleher Av, Mt Joy Ct (arbitrary). Result: part 1 from 3 automatic + 2 hand-picked junctions (4 along Wycoff Av.); part 2 from Kelleher/Wycoff plus 3 points carried from part 1 along match line A-B. Both drawn turned about 46 degrees.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 covers western central Ramsey at 100 ft to an inch, from Elbert at the left edge to Central Avenue and the Erie Railroad main line at the right. Darlington Road crosses the upper half diagonally from the top left to Central Avenue, with Elbert, Ackerman Avenue, Cherry Lane and North running south from it; Blauvelt Avenue crosses the sheet below them. Cherry Lane continues south past Shuart Road, marked Oak Street, and High School Place to Main, which runs east to Central Avenue; Wycoff Avenue continues the line of Main diagonally to the south-west, crossing Woodland Avenue at the lower left. South of Main, New runs south past an unnamed street to a second street lettered New, and Maple appears at the lower right beyond Central Avenue. The district is residential, with frame dwellings on regular lots, and holds several of the town's institutions: St. Paul's R. C. Church on Darlington Road, the Ramsey High School in brick on High School Place, the Ramsey Public School at Shuart Road and Central Avenue, and the First Presbyterian Church nearby. A concrete garage stands on Main west of New. Along the railroad at the upper right are the lumber shed, coal pocket and feed mill of the Rufner coal, feed, lumber and mason supplies yard. The lower left of the sheet holds the inset of part 2, outlined in a heavy line, and much of the area south of Wycoff Avenue is open land.
notes: Darlington Road is Darlington Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Shuart Road, also lettered Oak Street, is Shuart Lane; High School Place is School Street; Main is West Main Street; Wycoff Avenue is Wyckoff Avenue.
The street lettered 'Not Named' (block 57) south of Main is Pulis Lane today, and the lower east-west street lettered New is Cleveland Street.
The junction of Main, Cherry Lane and Wycoff Avenue has been rebuilt and was left out of the control.
Blauvelt Avenue is drawn about 25 ft wide against about 50 ft between today's parcels.
The sheet is drawn turned about 11 degrees from north.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Elbert, Ackerman Av, Darlington Rd, Blauvelt Av, Cherry Lane, Shuart Rd (Oak St), North, High School Pl, Main, New, Central Av, Wycoff Av, Woodland Av, Maple; Ramsey High School, Ramsey Public School, St Paul's R.C. Church. Part 2 (inset, left, outlined in a heavy line) Central Av, Broad, Maple, Not Named. Result: part 1 19 automatic points, RMSE 2.0 m, LOO 2.4 m; part 2 (inset, Broad and Prince Street) 4 automatic points, RMSE 0.2 m.

sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 6 is an inset in the left half of the sheet, outlined by a heavy line and drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows the blocks south of the main map along Central Avenue and Maple, from below Blauvelt Avenue on the sheet's main map down to an unnamed street at the bottom, with Broad crossing the two avenues in the middle. On the ground it lies south of the blocks shown on the main part, between Central Avenue and Maple around Broad, and not where it is placed on the page. Frame dwellings with small outbuildings line both sides of Central Avenue and Maple on narrow lots in blocks 29 and 30, with block 17 east of Maple and parts of blocks 31 and 32 west of Central Avenue, the latter mostly open. Water pipes run down Central Avenue and Maple and along the unnamed street, with hydrants at its corners.
notes: Central Avenue is South Central Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Broad is Broad Street; Maple is Maple Street.
The street lettered 'Not Named' at the bottom of the inset is Prince Street today.
Placed from four street junctions only (low redundancy).

Scale 100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Elbert, Ackerman Av, Darlington Rd, Blauvelt Av, Cherry Lane, Shuart Rd (Oak St), North, High School Pl, Main, New, Central Av, Wycoff Av, Woodland Av, Maple; Ramsey High School, Ramsey Public School, St Paul's R.C. Church. Part 2 (inset, left, outlined in a heavy line) Central Av, Broad, Maple, Not Named. Result: part 1 19 automatic points, RMSE 2.0 m, LOO 2.4 m; part 2 (inset, Broad and Prince Street) 4 automatic points, RMSE 0.2 m.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the eastern part of central Ramsey at 100 ft to an inch, east of the trolley right-of-way and the business blocks of sheets 2 and 3. Island Avenue runs north and south along the left side of the sheet, crossed by Carrol and Arch at its junction near the middle left, and Poplar crosses to the north. Arch runs diagonally from Island Avenue down to the Turnpike, which runs north and south along the right side; Finch and Christopher run between Poplar and Arch. Main crosses the sheet below the middle from the trolley right-of-way to the Turnpike, and Prospect runs diagonally across the lower part to the Turnpike, with the short Hart and an unnamed street at the bottom left. Lake Street and Airmount Avenue leave the Turnpike to the east. The area is mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings on deep lots, densest between Island Avenue, Poplar and Arch. Buildings of note are St. John's Protestant Church on Arch near the Turnpike, a large concrete garage on the south side of Main, an I.O.O.F. hall and a second hall on the Turnpike, a garage and the Ferncroft Road House at the corner of the Turnpike and Prospect, and a few small stores near the trolley crossing on Main. Much of the block between Main and Prospect, numbered 16, is open land. The trolley right-of-way runs north and south at the left edge, and water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the main streets.
notes: The Turnpike is Franklin Turnpike south of Main and North Franklin Turnpike north of it in OpenStreetMap.
Island Avenue is North Island Avenue south of Poplar in OpenStreetMap; Carrol is Carol Street; Main is East Main Street.
The junction of Main, Arch and the Turnpike has been rebuilt: Wyckoff Avenue now meets it, and the modern junctions there were not detected.
Island Avenue is drawn ending just south of Main; the modern North Island Avenue continues to Prospect.
The trolley right-of-way is lettered 'Trolly Right of Way'.

Scale 100 ft. Island Av, Carrol, Arch, Poplar, Finch, Christopher, Main, Turnpike, Lake St, Fairmount Av, Prospect, Hart, Not Named; trolley right-of-way. Result (pilot): 10 automatic points, RMSE 1.6 m, LOO 2.6 m; ink_below_paper 100 for the atlas.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the eastern edge of Ramsey at 100 ft to an inch, east of the Turnpike, which runs north and south along the left side of the sheet. Airmount leaves the Turnpike in the upper left and runs diagonally to the north-east corner, and De Baun branches from it to run east across the upper middle of the sheet. Crest Road runs south from De Baun to Lake, which crosses the lower part of the sheet from the Turnpike to the right edge; Terrace Drive and Holmes, the latter marked arbitrary, run south from Lake. Arch Street and Main Street meet the Turnpike at the lower left edge. The district is a thinly built residential subdivision: frame dwellings with small outbuildings stand along Airmount, De Baun, the Turnpike and Lake, and the blocks either side of Crest Road are divided into narrow building lots, most of them still empty. A small garage for five cars with gasoline tanks stands on the Turnpike at Airmount. In the lower right is the Ice Pond, marked dry in summer, with an ice house at its south-east corner, and the land east and south of it is open. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the Turnpike, Airmount, De Baun and Lake.
notes: The Turnpike is North Franklin Turnpike in OpenStreetMap; De Baun is DeBaun Avenue; Airmount is Airmount Avenue.
Terrace Drive is Bonnieview Terrace today, and Holmes, marked arbitrary on the sheet, is Dixon Street.
The Ice Pond is marked dry in summer.
The sheet is drawn turned about 13 degrees from north, more than the neighbouring sheet 7 (about 7 degrees).

Scale 100 ft. Turnpike, Airmount, De Baun, Crest Rd, Lake, Terrace Drive, Holmes (arbitrary), Arch St, Main St; Ice Pond. Result: 6 automatic points, RMSE 1.7 m, LOO 3.2 m; drawn turned about 13 degrees.
